## Vision — The Behavioral Sales Operating System | Bylda

Source: https://usebylda.com/vision

The Long View

# The behavioral sales operating system.

Bylda today audits sales behavior and tells teams what to change. This page is the longer arc — where that goes, in what order, and an honest account of what does not ship yet.

## The premise

Sales software has spent three decades getting very good at recording activity. Calls logged, stages advanced, tasks created, deals closed. It was a reasonable architecture for a world where the only account of what happened inside a conversation was the memory of the person who had it.

The consequence is that the most important variable in revenue — how people actually behave — has never been a data type. Every forecast, every coaching decision, and every process change has been made on top of a record that describes outcomes and says nothing about conduct.

Sales teams have been measuring activity for decades. The thing worth measuring was always behavior.

That constraint has genuinely lifted. A model can now read a conversation the way an experienced manager does — the question that was never asked, the objection answered too fast, the order things happened in — and do it on every call, every day. So behavior becomes measurable, and once it is measurable it can be connected to outcomes and learned from. That is the whole thesis, and everything below follows from it.

The progression

## Observe. Understand. Recommend.

Then execute.

In that order, deliberately. Each phase depends on the data the previous one produces, and skipping ahead would mean automating decisions nothing has validated.

PHASE 1 · NOW

Intelligence

Call review, behavior analysis, rep profiles, daily briefs, coaching and results.

Shipping. This is what you buy today.

PHASE 2 · NEXT

Workflow

Behavioral context living inside the workflow: pipeline intelligence, accounts, playbooks built from what actually works.

In development. Not sold as shipped.

PHASE 3 · LATER

Execution

Acting on the intelligence: automated follow-up, workflow execution, revenue optimization.

Research direction. Years, not quarters.

THROUGHOUT

Learning

Every phase feeds the Behavior Graph, which is what makes the next phase possible.

Compounds from day one.

THE POINT

Order matters

You cannot automate an action you have not yet shown to work.

Which is why Phase 1 is not a stepping stone. It is the foundation.

Honest accounting

## What ships today.

What doesn't, yet.

Shipping now

✓ Call review: stages, events, talk and control on one timeline

✓ Analysis that names where the call was lost, with the quote as evidence

✓ Behavior profiles for each rep against the team and their own baseline

✓ Daily briefs for reps and managers, and the coach queue

✓ Assigned coaching and behavior change results, with confidence stated

Where we're going — not shipped

→ Behavioral context written back into the CRM

→ Weekly and team reports, and Slack or Teams delivery of briefs

→ Behavioral models calibrated across many resolved outcomes

→ Controlled comparison of coaching interventions

→ Native pipeline and account workflows

→ Playbooks generated from measured outcomes

→ Automated follow-up and workflow execution

Things Bylda does not claim, and will not: prediction of individual deal outcomes with certainty, proof of causation from observed association, tone, emotion or sentiment readings presented as fact, guaranteed revenue uplift, or autonomous selling. We would rather be trusted than sound futuristic.

## Why the order cannot be reversed

The tempting version of this company starts at Phase 3: an agent that runs the sales process. It does not work, for a reason that is structural rather than technical. To automate a commercial action responsibly you need evidence that the action produces the outcome you want, in your market, with your buyers. That evidence does not exist anywhere yet — it has to be created, one resolved outcome at a time.

Auditing behavior is how you create it. So Phase 1 is not a wedge we tolerate until the interesting work starts; it is the only way the interesting work becomes possible. The Behavior Graph is the asset being built, and it accrues whether or not anyone is thinking about Phase 3.

## What stays true in every phase

We sit on top of your stack. Your CRM remains the system of record. Bylda is the system of intelligence. Replacing your CRM has never been the plan.

Every claim is traceable. If Bylda says a behavior happened, it can point at the moment. A finding you cannot verify is an assertion.

We show our evidence. Conduct, tone, emotion and sentiment are each tied to a moment you can replay, with confidence stated. Signals, not verdicts.

Your data is yours. Conversations never train shared models — see our security posture .

Reps come first. A tool a sales team resents produces gamed behavior and worthless data. No leaderboards.

## Start with the part

that works today.

Audit a week of your team's conversations. Everything else compounds from there.

## About Bylda — Why We Measure Sales Behavior

Source: https://usebylda.com/about

About

# Sales software measured activity.

It never measured behavior.

Bylda exists because the variable that decides revenue — how people actually conduct themselves in a conversation — has never been something software could see.

## The observation

Sit with a sales manager on a Friday and watch them try to work out why one rep is at 140% and another at 60%. They have the activity data. Calls made, meetings booked, pipeline created, win rate, deal velocity. All of it accurate, none of it explanatory.

So they do the only thing available: they listen to a few calls. Five, maybe, out of the three hundred the team had that week. Whatever is systematically going wrong is, by arithmetic, mostly happening in the 295 they never hear.

Then they coach from that sample, and everyone involved knows it is a sample.

The information was always there. It was in the conversations. Nobody had the hours to go and find it.

## What changed

Two things, recently and quietly. Almost every sales conversation is now recorded by default. And models can now read a conversation the way an experienced manager does — noticing the question that was never asked, the objection answered too quickly, the order things happened in — rather than just transcribing the words.

Those two facts together make behavior measurable for the first time. Not inferred from a survey, not self-reported in a CRM field, but observed directly, on every conversation, every day.

## What we decided to build

Not a better recorder — recording is commoditized and was never the valuable part. Not another dashboard — the world does not need more numbers without reasons.

We built the layer that reads what is underneath the record. We call it the Phantom Layer: the behavioral stratum beneath the visible pipeline, always present, never previously captured. Bylda audits it continuously and returns findings a person can act on today.

The category name for this is behavioral sales intelligence , and the longer arc — including a plain account of what does not ship yet — is on our vision page .

Principles

## Five positions we will not trade.

Every claim is traceable. If Bylda says a behavior happened, it points at the moment. A finding you cannot verify is an assertion, and assertions do not change how anyone sells.

Signals, not verdicts. Bylda reads conduct, tone, emotion and sentiment, and every reading is tied to a moment you can replay, with its confidence. No personality typing. A reading you cannot check is an assertion, and a rep who feels judged by a score learns to game it.

Reps come first. A rep sees their own audit before their manager does. No leaderboards. A tool a sales team resents produces gamed behavior and worthless data, which defeats the entire point.

Your data is yours. Conversations never train shared or third-party models. That is contractual, not a policy page — the Behavior Graph built from your data belongs to you.

We say what it does not do. On this site, on demos, and when the honest answer is that we are not the right fit yet.

## Why "Phantom"

Not because anything is spooky. Because the most important information in a sales process has been invisible — present in every conversation, recorded by nobody, acted on by almost no one. Phantom is what we call the intelligence that was always there and finally became legible.

We use the word sparingly and only where it means something: the Phantom Layer and the Phantom Audit . Everything else in the product has a normal name, because renaming ordinary things is how companies become tiresome.

## Where we are

Early, and honest about it. Bylda is opening access in waves to B2B sales organizations where calls are recorded, a CRM is in use, and a manager has more reps than listening hours. If that is you, the fastest way to evaluate us is to bring a week of real conversations and see whether the findings are ones you would have reached yourself with unlimited time.

## Bring a week of real calls.

That is genuinely the whole evaluation. Either the findings are useful or they are not.

Request access →

Read the vision

## Security — How Bylda Handles Conversation Data | Bylda

Source: https://usebylda.com/security

Security

# Your conversations

stay yours.

Bylda reads the most sensitive thing your company owns: what customers and reps actually say to each other. This page states what we commit to, plainly, including the part about your own team.

## No training on your data

Your conversations are never used to train shared or third-party models.

## Encrypted

Encrypted in transit and at rest.

## Reps see their own first

A rep sees their own findings before their manager reads them. No peer leaderboards.

## Signals, not verdicts

Tone, emotion and sentiment are shown as signals tied to a moment you can replay, with confidence stated. Bylda does not type personalities.

## Evidence you can check

Every finding points to the moment in the call, with its sample size and confidence.

## Deletion is real

Remove a conversation and the findings derived from it go with it.

The line we don't cross

## Isolation is the default.

Every customer's data lives in a logically isolated tenant with its own encryption context. Models read your data to serve you, in your session, and nothing crosses that boundary.

No shared embeddings between tenants

No human review of your transcripts without written, per-incident consent

Security review On request

Data processing agreement On request

Security questionnaire On request

Subprocessor list On request

Questions from your security team security@usebylda.com

Questions we get asked

## Answered plainly.

Does Bylda record calls without consent? +

Bylda does not record calls itself. It analyzes recordings your recorder, dialer or CRM already produced, or that you upload, so recording consent stays with the tool that records them.

Who inside our company can see a given call? +

Reps see their own calls and findings. Managers see their team. Reps never see peer rankings.

What happens to our data if we leave? +

You can ask us to export and delete your data, and we confirm in writing when deletion is done.

Which model providers process our conversations? +

Ask us for the current subprocessor list. Your conversations are never used to train shared or third-party models.

## The commitment about your own team

Most security pages stop at customer data. Bylda analyzes how your employees work, so there is a second set of commitments that belongs here.

Reps see their own audit first. A rep is never in a position where their manager has read a finding about them that they have not seen.

Findings are signals, not verdicts. Bylda reports what was said and done and how it sounded, with the timestamp and a confidence level. It does not rate people or type personalities.

No leaderboards. Ranking reps against each other produces gamed behavior and worse data, which defeats the purpose of measuring at all.

Deletion is real. Remove a conversation and the derived traces, signals and audit findings go with it.

This is not only an ethics position. A workforce-analytics deployment that a sales team resents gets worked around, and worked-around measurement is worthless. See what a rep actually sees .
